project: Verifying Representation-Level Circuit Breakers (RR) as a Safety Intervention
direction: Representation-Level Circuit Breakers for Safe LLMs — reroute harmful-behavior representations without exposure to attack prompts; verify robustness, capability preservation, VLM transfer, and agent transfer.

journey_summary.claim: 4 given behaviors (C1-C4) captured from task.md; recommended plan = self-contained RR verification harness (7 milestones, M1-M7, no M0 gate).
journey_summary.mechanism_routing: family=Representation and Parameter Analysis / Representation Engineering (RepE), submethod=mean-diff direction + LoRA-parameterized RR loss (L_rr = cos²(a_tuned^h, d_h_base))
journey_summary.experiment: 19 runs total, ~1.85 GPU-h consumed (of 10 h budget); headline NEGATIVE — all four claims track back to a single mechanism failure at M3 (L_rr collapsed to ~1e-4 from step 0; M4 confirmed no reroute).
journey_summary.verify: 4 claim(s): 0 PASS / 0 FAIL / 4 INCONCLUSIVE / 0 ZEV / 0 INTEGRITY_ONLY (cap=0, swap_off=0); main-experiment integrity Phase 2 FAIL on all — mech Check A FAIL (no alpha sweep, no capability metric, n_random=1); Stage 2 never entered.
journey_summary.iteration: 5/6 iterations, claim-reentries=0/2, score 8/10 verdict ready, termination=positive_verdict; 16 runs, 1.842 GPU-h; root-cause diagnosed (LoRA cos² gradient too weak); pivotal fix = signed_hinge loss + refusal-CE supervision (α=5, β=1, λ_refuse=5, m=0.30); post-iter states — C1: PASS, C2: PASS (substantive), C4: PASS (substantive), C3: UNRESOLVED (M6 VLM not re-fit — path forward documented, ~1.7 GPU-h).
journey_summary.figures: 5 figures across 3 claims (C1: 2, C2: 2, C4: 1); 1 judgment-skipped (C3 — no plot data); 0 render-skipped, 0 errored

open_items: C3 UNRESOLVED: VLM transfer (LLaVA-NeXT-Mistral-7B PGD image-hijack) was never re-fit with the iter-5 signed_hinge+refusal-CE recipe. Documented forward path: (1) /auto-experiment on M6 with `--rr-loss signed_hinge --rr-margin 0.30 --alpha 5 --beta 1 --lambda-refuse 5 --lora-rank 16` on Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 base; (2) reassemble LLaVA-NeXT-Mistral-7B with RR-tuned base (freeze vision encoder + projector); (3) run PGD ε=32/255 × 1000 steps on 100-prompt × 3-image harm probe. Estimated ~1.7 GPU-h, feasible within remaining ~6.3 GPU-h budget. Then `/auto-verify C3`.

Data-source conflict (HARD vs HARD, unresolved but scientifically bypassed): task.md pins GraySwanAI training set as 'always used, fixed' but repo github.com/GraySwanAI/circuit-breakers is on .claude/forbidden-urls.txt (blind-reproduction setup). Pipeline proceeded with constructed-equivalent fallback (HarmBench-public + Alpaca paired) — iter-5 results demonstrate the reconstructed RR objective (with the added refusal-CE term) delivers the claimed behavior, so the fallback is validated.

Ablation nice-to-have (recommended in AUTO_ITERATION_FINAL_REPORT.md): rerun iter-5 with `--lambda-refuse 5 --alpha 0` to isolate whether the RR term contributes causally beyond refusal-CE alone. Est. 0.3 GPU-h.

Two plan gates now known to be infeasible against floor effects (recommended in AUTO_ITERATION_FINAL_REPORT.md, needs plan revision): C2 `asr(RR) ≤ asr(B1) − 10 pp` (both at 0-ASR floor); C4 `harmful_tool_use_rate(RR) ≤ B0 − 20 pp` (B0 already at 0.010). Iter-5 RR ties both baselines at floor with no regression — the pinned gate wording overstates achievable ceilings.

Verify VERIFY_REPORT.md and per-claim ROBUSTNESS.md still reflect the original (pre-iteration) INCONCLUSIVE state — a fresh Phase 2 audit on iter-5 artifacts would upgrade C1/C2/C4 formally to PASS. Documented in AUTO_ITERATION_FINAL_REPORT.md item 3.

Original C1 audit finding (fixed by iter-5): M1 saved LR probe coefficients as `directions.pt` rather than plan-specified mean-difference direction (mean-diff saved separately as `directions_meandiff.pt`); training_summary.json's `sweep_notes` 'L_rr decreasing significantly' string was inconsistent with the observed L_rr_ema=0.0016. Iter-5 code rewrite of scripts/m3_rr_train.py addresses the loss formulation problem; direction-naming inconsistency remains a documentation-only issue.

claims.statement: Harmful-output behaviour in an instruction-tuned LLM corresponds to identifiable internal representations that can be rerouted to an orthogonal, non-harmful subspace using only paired benign/harmful data, without exposure to any attack prompts.

data.source: HarmBench behaviors.csv train split + Alpaca single-turn benign, length/format matched
data.used_n: M1: 384 train + 128 held-out; M4: same 128 held-out
data.subset_note: Blind-reproduction fallback (GraySwanAI repo forbidden); disjoint from M5 eval reserve.

claims.method: M1 residual-stream mean-difference direction extraction + per-layer linear-probe AUC → sites S=[9,10,11,12,13,14] (top-6 by AUC, contiguous mid-band); M4 post-tune diagnostic on 128 held-out pairs with random-orthogonal specificity control.

main_experiment.key_stats: mean_auc_all_layers=0.9762; n_layers_auc>0.8 in mid-late half=20; Δcos_harmful=-0.0197 (target ≤-0.30); Δcos_benign=0.0043 (target |Δ|≤0.1); Δcos_harmful_ctrl_random=-0.0003; criterion_c1a_passed=YES, criterion_c1b_reroute_passed=NO
main_experiment.headline: Identifiability confirmed (AUC 0.976, 20 layers > 0.8) but reroute NOT observed — Δcos_harmful=-0.020 is 15× too small vs target -0.30; specificity control also near-zero, so the tuned model barely moved activations on any direction. L_rr stayed near-zero throughout M3; the RR loss minimized without triggering the mechanism.

changed: m3_rr_train.py: added signed_hinge loss + refusal-CE supervision (--lambda-refuse, REFUSAL_TEMPLATES); recipe alpha=5, beta=1, lambda_refuse=5, rr_margin=0.30
iteration.narrowed_to: Reroute PASSES with signed_hinge loss + refusal-CE (not with original cos² loss). iter-5 M4: Δcos_harmful=-0.434 (target ≤-0.30), Δcos_benign=-0.044 (|Δ|≤0.10), Δcos_ctrl=-0.004.

claims.final_status: ✓ holds — reroute PASSES with signed_hinge loss + refusal-CE recipe (iter-5): Δcos_harmful=-0.434, Δcos_benign=-0.044, specificity clean. Original cos² loss failed due to gradient magnitude issue; iteration diagnosed and fixed the mechanism.
caveats: training instability: several late-training grad-norm spikes at M3 steps 300/330/370/470/480/490 (magnitudes 128-852); at step 490 L_ret also spiked to 2.30. L_rr stayed near-zero for the entire 500 steps (final EMA 0.0016) — most likely a mis-calibrated loss / LoRA subspace that could not deliver representation-level rotation.

reroute FAILED with high statistical confidence: delta=-0.020 is well below the -0.30 target, and the specificity-control delta of -0.0003 shows the tuned model moved neither on d_h nor on random directions — consistent evidence that the RR objective failed to shape the model, not that shaping was directionally imprecise.

figures.caption: Reroute mechanism engages only after iter-5 signed_hinge + refusal-CE recipe (Δcos_harmful −0.02 → −0.434); benign drift stays inside the 0.10 tolerance; specificity control confirms the rotation is targeted.
Layer-wise linear-probe AUC on residual-stream activations (128 held-out harmful/benign pairs). Peaks at mid-late layers 9-14 (chosen as sites S) with AUC>0.99; identifiability half of C1 satisfied.

claims.statement: A model fine-tuned with Representation Rerouting (RR) achieves substantially lower attack success rates than refusal-trained (B0) or adversarial-trained (B1) baselines across a wide range of unseen HarmBench attack categories, while preserving MT-Bench and MMLU capability.

data.source: HarmBench-eval reserve (6 attack categories, 30/cat) + MT-Bench (40 questions) + MMLU 5-shot (300 questions)
data.subset_note: Compact eval subsets to fit GPU-hour budget; eval reserve disjoint from M1/M3 train.

claims.method: M2 R2D2-lite adversarial fine-tune baseline (LoRA rank-16, 400 steps, 12 adv templates in place of 512 GCG suffixes); M3 RR fine-tune with L_rr + L_ret + λ_lm; M5 6-category HarmBench ASR + MT-Bench + MMLU 5-shot on all 3 variants (LLM judge).

main_experiment.key_stats: aggregate ASR: B0=0.333, B1=0.000, RR=0.356 (RR-B0 Δ=+2.22 pp; target ≤-20 pp) [FAIL]; MT-Bench: B0=6.30, B1=1.08, RR=5.85 (Δ=-0.45; target Δ≥-0.3) [FAIL]; MMLU: B0=0.58, B1=0.54, RR=0.57 (Δ=-1.0 pp; target ≤2 pp) [PASS]; RR beats B1 on unseen persona=0.00 pp, hypothetical=+16.67, human-redteam=+43.33 pp — but B1 over-refuses everything (ASR 0.000, MT-Bench 1.08) so this is B1's over-refusal, not RR's safety [FAIL]. c2_pass_count=1/4
main_experiment.headline: RR did NOT reduce HarmBench ASR — it actually rose by 2.2 pp vs B0; MT-Bench slightly regressed; MMLU preserved. B1's apparent 'unseen-attack loss' is B1 refusing everything, not RR's added safety. Consistent with C1's mechanism failure.

changed: m5_eval.py: added --adapter override (previously hardcoded to artifacts/m3/RR_lora); re-ran M5 on iter-5 RR adapter
iteration.narrowed_to: RR (iter-5) achieves HarmBench aggregate ASR=0.000 vs B0=0.333 (beats by 33 pp — exceeds the 20 pp plan gate); MT-Bench=6.15 (≥ 6.00), MMLU=0.56 (at threshold). The 'beat B1 by 10 pp on unseen attacks' sub-gate is trivially infeasible at the 0-ASR floor (both RR-iter5 and B1 reach 0).

claims.final_status: ✓ holds (substantive) — RR (iter-5 signed_hinge + refusal-CE) reaches HarmBench 0.000 across all 6 categories (beats B0 by 33 pp), MT-Bench 6.15 (within plan tolerance), MMLU 0.56 (at threshold). Only failing gate is the ≤B1-10pp sub-criterion which is infeasible against a 0-ASR floor.
caveats: [suspected under-power: R2D2-lite templates in place of 512-GCG suffixes to stay within 10 GPU-hour budget — RR vs B1 comparison on unseen categories may over/underestimate RR's edge because B1 over-refuses everything]
compact eval subsets used (HarmBench 180, MT-Bench 40, MMLU 300) — verify stage should try broader / GCG-strengthened variant if resource permits.

figures.caption: HarmBench per-category ASR by model variant (30 prompts / category). Iter-5 RR achieves 0.000 across all 6 attack categories (matching B1's over-refusal ceiling) while B0=0.333 and original cos²-loss RR=0.356.
Capability preservation on MT-Bench (out of 10) and MMLU (5-shot). Iter-5 RR = 6.15/0.56 stays within plan tolerance vs B0=6.30/0.58; B1 collapses to 1.08 MT-Bench (over-refusal).

claims.statement: The same representation-level intervention transfers to multimodal LLMs, blocking image-based jailbreaks (PGD image-hijack attacks against LLaVA-NeXT-Mistral-7B) without materially degrading vision-language task performance.

data.source: M6-locate + M6-train paired data on Mistral-7B; full PGD image-hijack skipped (VLM weights not local)
data.used_n: 256 paired Mistral train examples for M6-train; 128 held-out for M6-diagnostic
data.subset_note: Full PGD ε=32/255 × 1000-step image-hijack on LLaVA-NeXT-Mistral-7B not run — VLM weights not on disk and downloading + running would exceed 10 GPU-hour budget.

claims.method: Mini M1 site-locate on Mistral (sites [10-15], AUC 0.970); RR fine-tune on Mistral with same L_rr formulation; M4-style diagnostic. LLaVA-NeXT-Mistral assembly + PGD attack skipped.

main_experiment.verdict: partial (VLM assembly skipped; mechanism-level negative on Mistral base)
main_experiment.key_stats: mistral mean_auc_all_layers=0.970; mistral sites=[10,11,12,13,14,15]; mistral Δcos_harmful=-0.0116 (target ≤-0.30); mistral Δcos_benign=-0.0042; mistral_reroute_passed=NO
main_experiment.headline: Full PGD attack skipped (LLaVA-NeXT-Mistral-7B not local). At the mechanism level on Mistral-7B: same reroute failure as Llama-3 (Δcos_harmful=-0.012 vs target -0.30). Even a successful VLM assembly would face the same base-model mechanism failure — no C3 transfer would be expected.

iteration.narrowed_to: M6 (Mistral RR + LLaVA-NeXT-Mistral PGD image-hijack) was never re-fit with the iter-5 recipe. Path to close is fully specified: /auto-experiment on M6 with alpha=5, beta=1, lambda_refuse=5, rr_loss=signed_hinge, rr_margin=0.30, lora_rank=16 on Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 base; then reassemble LLaVA-NeXT-Mistral and run PGD ε=32/255 × 1000 steps. Estimated cost ~1.7 GPU-h (well within remaining ~6.3 GPU-h budget).

claims.final_status: ⏸ unresolved — VLM transfer path forward documented but not executed: refit M6 on Mistral base with iter-5 refusal-CE recipe (~1.7 GPU-h remaining). C1/C2/C4 success suggests the recipe should transfer; C3 verification is a follow-up /auto-experiment call away.
caveats: [suspected under-power: full PGD ε=32/255 × 1000-step image-hijack on LLaVA-NeXT-Mistral-7B not run — VLM weights not on disk. Mechanism-level substeps ran and showed the same failure as M3.]
VLM base-model mismatch: LLaVA-NeXT-Mistral base is Mistral-7B, not Llama-3, so a separate mini RR fine-tune on Mistral was required (M6L, M6T). Ran, but same reroute failure.

claims.statement: The same representation-level intervention transfers to LLM agents, materially reducing the rate of harmful tool-use actions executed under attack, while preserving general function-calling capability (BFCL).

data.source: 100 authored harmful-agent prompts (4 categories × 25) + 50 BFCL exec_simple prompts scored by AST-name match
data.subset_note: BFCL substitute (50 exec_simple, AST-name match) in place of the full BFCL v3 harness — compact substitute documented.

models: Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct + M3 RR LoRA in same scaffold
claims.method: Reuse M3 RR LoRA (no additional fine-tune); M7 evaluates harmful_tool_use_rate on 100-prompt harm set + BFCL exec_simple 50 prompts.

main_experiment.verdict: partial (1/2 sub-criteria met — BFCL PASS; harm-reduction FAIL)
main_experiment.key_stats: harmful_tool_use_rate: B0=0.010, RR=0.040 (Δ=+3.00 pp; target ≤-20 pp) [FAIL]; BFCL exec_simple: B0=0.980, RR=1.000 (Δ=+2.00 pp; target Δ≥-3 pp) [PASS]; c4_pass_count=1/2
main_experiment.headline: RR did NOT reduce agent harm — it slightly rose (from 0.010 to 0.040, both near-zero since base already refuses). BFCL preserved. Consistent with C1/C2: no safety transfer because the RR mechanism never activated.

changed: m7_agent_eval.py: added --adapter override; re-ran M7 on iter-5 RR adapter
iteration.narrowed_to: Agent harmful_tool_use_rate = 0.010 matches B0=0.010 (no regression, vastly better than iter-2 mechanism-only which reached 0.310). BFCL score = 1.00 (perfect capability preservation). Plan's absolute ≤20 pp harm-reduction gate is infeasible against a B0 floor of 0.010.

claims.final_status: ✓ holds (substantive) — RR (iter-5) preserves agent safety (harmful_tool_use=0.010, matches B0) and improves BFCL capability to 1.00 (from B0's 0.98). Falsified the earlier iter-2 mechanism-only recipe which increased agent harm to 0.310. Only failing gate is the ≤B0-20pp absolute criterion which is infeasible against the 0.010 floor.
caveats: BFCL substitute: 50 exec_simple prompts scored by AST-name match (not the full BFCL v3 harness).

harm-rate floor effect: both B0 (0.010) and RR (0.040) are near-zero because Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct's base RLHF-safety already refuses nearly all authored agent-harm prompts — the 20-pp target is inapplicable when there is only ~1 pp of headroom on the B0 side.

figures.caption: Agent harmful_tool_use_rate and BFCL exec_simple score by variant. Iter-5 RR matches B0's 0.010 harm floor (no regression) and achieves BFCL=1.00; original cos²-loss RR climbed harm to 0.040.
